title: All six identity fields
priority: Must fix before release
problem: Refused requests are not audited, and gateway denials may lack identity fields.
steps: 1. Open `src/main.py` and in `chat` at line 113 add an audit row for the 401 with event `auth_refused` and the six identity fields. 2. Do the same in `confirm` near line 139. 3. Open `src/gateway.py` line 132. For an unknown actor, write `untrusted_caller` instead of `unknown` and keep the header values. 4. Make `_log` raise if the insert fails, at line 133, so the request is refused. 5. Add a test that a bad token creates one audit row.
done_when: A request with a bad token leaves an audit row with the six identity fields.

title: Content-derived type identity
priority: Must fix before release
problem: The type ID code looks sound, but nobody has shown that each input changes it.
steps: 1. Run `python -m src.type_id sha256:<64 hex digits>` from the repo root and save the output. 2. Run it again and check the ID is the same. 3. Change one input at a time: the digest, the model id in `config/agent.yaml`, a prompt line, a `src` file, `requirements.txt`, `Dockerfile`. Run it after each. 4. Check each change gives a new ID, and undo it. 5. Create `tests/test_type_id.py` that does these checks with temporary copies of the files.
done_when: Changing any single input produces a different agent-type-id and the same input gives the same ID.

title: Trustworthy attribution
priority: Must fix before release
problem: The gateway trusts an instance header from the caller, and an approval resume starts a new trace.
steps: 1. Open `src/gateway.py` line 170. Stop reading the instance from `x-agent-instance`. 2. Ask the identity team to add an `instance` claim to tokens made by `src/credentials.py` line 47. Read it from `claims` instead. 3. In `migrations/001_init.sql` line 54 add a `traceparent text` column to `approvals.grants`. 4. Store it in `src/approvals.py` line 46 and restore it in `src/agent.py` line 124 when resuming. 5. Add a test that a forged `x-agent-instance` header is ignored.
done_when: A caller cannot choose the instance used for stop and rate decisions, and a resumed run keeps its trace.

title: Operational lookup
priority: Must fix before release
problem: Stopping an agent type is not enforced at the gateway, and its audit rows hold caller-supplied IDs.
steps: 1. Do B04 first, which adds the agent-type stop check. 2. Ask the identity team to put the `agent_type_id` in the STS token. 3. In `src/gateway.py` line 138 write the token value, not the header, into the audit row. 4. In `migrations/001_init.sql` lines 23, rename `agent_type_id_hint` and `agent_instance_hint` to `agent_type_id` and `agent_instance_id`. 5. Add a test that a forged header value is not stored.
done_when: Gateway audit rows hold IDs taken from the verified token.

title: Minimal tool surface
priority: Must fix before release
problem: The escalate tool can skip the gateway and call the helpdesk server directly.
steps: 1. Open `config/tools.yaml` and delete the `direct_route:` block under `escalate_to_human` (lines 91-93). 2. Open `src/gateway_client.py`. In `call`, delete the whole `except GatewayUnavailable:` block (lines 51-59) so a gateway outage raises an error. 3. Run `grep -rn direct_route src config` and check it prints nothing. 4. Add a test that makes the gateway return 503 for `escalate_to_human`. It should raise `GatewayUnavailable` and make no second call.
done_when: When the gateway is down, `escalate_to_human` fails and no call is sent to the helpdesk server.

title: Least-privilege access
priority: Must fix before release
problem: One employee's private handbook results can be served to another employee from the search cache.
steps: 1. Open `src/retrieval.py` and go to `_key` at line 40. Change its signature to `def _key(self, query: str, employee_id: str) -> str:`. 2. In `_key`, change line 42 so the hashed text is `f"{self._top_k}|{employee_id}|{normalized}"`. 3. In `search`, change line 46 to `key = self._key(query, employee_id)`. 4. Create `tests/test_retrieval_cache.py`. Call `search` twice with the same query and two employee ids, using a fake pool. Check the second call runs its own query. 5. Ask the platform team for the IAM and STS policy exports that show each credential is limited to its tenant and audience. Attach them to the B02 record.
done_when: Two employees who send the same query never share a cached result.

title: Independent revocation
priority: Must fix before release
problem: The gateway stop check ignores agent type, and tokens stay valid for 300 seconds after a stop.
steps: 1. Do the B01 fix first so no call skips the gateway. 2. Open `src/gateway.py` and go to `_stop_reason` at line 97. In the SQL add `OR (scope = 'agent_type' AND value = $4)` before the closing parenthesis. 3. In the same call at line 102 add a fourth argument `request_agent_type`, and pass it from `mcp` at line 171. 4. Set `TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS` in `src/credentials.py` line 20 to the longest stop time the owners accept, for example 60. 5. Add a test that sets an `agent_type` stop flag and checks the gateway returns 403 `stopped`.
done_when: A stop flag for the agent type makes the gateway refuse the next call.

title: Destructive-action interception
priority: Must fix before release
problem: The employee approves a leave request but is not shown the note that is sent with it.
steps: 1. Open `src/approvals.py` and go to `describe` at line 29. 2. In the leave branch, add `f" Note: {args.get('note') or 'none'}."` before the sentence about the manager. 3. Create `tests/test_approvals.py` with a test that calls `describe` with a note and checks the note text is in the result. 4. Run `python -m pytest tests/test_approvals.py`.
done_when: The approval text for a leave request contains the note field.

title: Approval integrity
priority: Must fix before release
problem: The approval screen leaves out one argument that is later sent.
steps: 1. Open `src/approvals.py` and go to `describe` at line 29. 2. Make the leave branch print `leave_type`, `start_date`, `end_date` and `note`, so every approved argument is shown. 3. Create `tests/test_approvals.py` and add a test that every key in the tool input schema appears in the text from `describe`. 4. Run `python -m pytest tests/test_approvals.py`.
done_when: The approval description shows every argument that the approval hash covers.

title: Match release identity to running state
priority: Must fix before release
problem: Only the agent checks its own identity. Nothing outside it compares the running setup with the manifest.
steps: 1. Open `k8s/admission.yaml`. Add a Kyverno rule that checks the pod's `AGENT_TYPE_ID` env value equals the value in the signed release manifest. 2. Or create a scheduled job that reads the pod's env and the stamped `release/manifest.yaml` and alerts on a difference. 3. Deploy it in a test cluster with a changed `AGENT_TYPE_ID`. It must be refused or alerted.
done_when: A pod whose ID differs from the manifest is blocked or raises an alert.

title: Recursive shutdown
priority: Must fix before release
problem: Stop sets a flag, but 300 second tokens stay valid and the direct route skips the stop check.
steps: 1. Do B01 first. 2. Open `src/credentials.py` line 20. Lower `TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS` to the stop time the owners set, for example 60. 3. In `src/credentials.py` line 68, call `drop_subject` when a stop flag is seen in `src/killswitch.py` line 56. 4. Write the in-flight tool calls into the audit log at stop, in `src/main.py` line 91. 5. Run a stop drill and record the longest time before calls fail.
done_when: After a stop, the next gateway call fails within the stated time.

title: Audit across service boundaries
priority: Must fix before release
problem: Gateway audit rows lack verified identity, a trace link and a vendor ID, and are written after the call.
steps: 1. Do B01 and A05 first. 2. Open `src/gateway.py` line 177. Before the upstream call add `await _log(request, claims, tool, "allow", "forwarding")`. 3. At line 190, write the vendor receipt id from the upstream response into the audit row. 4. Add `vendor_request_id` and `agent_instance_id` columns to `audit.gateway_decisions` in `migrations/001_init.sql` line 20. 5. Add a test that a call writes its audit row before the upstream call.
done_when: Each gateway audit row has the verified IDs, the trace and the vendor ID, and is written before forwarding.

title: Tested kill switch
priority: Must fix before release
problem: The stop check can be skipped by the direct route and is not run before each tool call.
steps: 1. Do B01 first so no call skips the gateway. 2. Open `src/agent.py` and in `_handle_tool` add `await self.stop.raise_if_stopped(ctx)` after line 105, before the tool runs. 3. Create a test that sets a stop flag during a run. No tool call must be sent after it. 4. Run a stop drill in staging, and write down the date and the time to stop. 5. Create `docs/stop-drill.md` and save the drill record in it.
done_when: After a stop flag is set, no new tool call is sent and a dated drill proves it.

title: Safe state after stopping
priority: Must fix before release
problem: There is no per-tool rule for work in progress at stop, and unknown outcomes are not held.
steps: 1. Open `config/tools.yaml` and add `on_stop: cancel` to `get_leave_balance` and `search_policies`, and `on_stop: hold_for_review` to `file_leave_request` and `escalate_to_human`. 2. Open `src/agent.py` line 185. When a `ToolError` has status 504, write an audit event `outcome_unknown` with the operation id. 3. Block a repeat of that operation until a person clears it. Check `outcome_unknown` rows in `_handle_tool` before line 120. 4. Add a test that a 504 on `file_leave_request` blocks an identical second request.
done_when: An unknown outcome blocks a repeat of the same action until a person clears it.

title: Full execution audit
priority: Must fix before release
problem: Some tool calls and cancelled calls leave no linked audit step.
steps: 1. Open `src/agent.py` line 154. Before the call add `await self.audit.record(ctx, "proposed_action", step_id=sid, tool="hris/get_leave_balance")` with a new `sid = str(uuid.uuid4())`. 2. After the call at line 156, record `tool_result` with the same `sid`. 3. In `src/gateway_client.py` line 54, record the retry before sending. Remove it if B01 is done. 4. In `src/main.py` line 91, record a `tool_cancelled` event with the pending `step_id`. 5. Add a test that every `proposed_action` has a later result, denial or cancel row.
done_when: Every proposed action has a linked outcome row, including failed or cancelled ones.

title: Credential lifetime and handling
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: Some secrets are fixed keys and the repository does not show their rotation or lifetime.
steps: 1. Ask the platform team for the rotation policy of secrets `hr-agent-db`, `hr-gateway-db` and `hr-agent-anthropic` used in `k8s/deployment.yaml`. 2. Ask them if the database supports short-lived or federated logins, and write the answer down. 3. Ask the identity team for an STS token sample showing the `cnf` field on downstream tokens. 4. Write the lifetime and revocation gap of each static key in `release/manifest.yaml` under `permissions`. 5. Check that each secret has a dated rotation record. The platform team confirms this.
done_when: Each static secret has a recorded owner, rotation period and revocation gap.

title: Hard execution budgets
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: Limits were not shown to hold with parallel runs, retries and charging order.
steps: 1. Open `src/agent.py` line 70 and see that the model call can retry inside the SDK. Change `AsyncAnthropic(max_retries=1)` to `max_retries=0` at `src/main.py` line 172. 2. Open `src/budgets.py` line 104 (`reserve_run`) and read how tokens are charged after each call. 3. Add a test that starts 30 runs at once for one user. The user quota of 150 runs and 400000 tokens must hold. 4. Add a test where usage is just under a limit and one more call is made. It must stop with `BudgetExceeded`. 5. Record the worst-case overshoot as a number in `config/agent.yaml` near line 18.
done_when: A test shows that parallel runs and retries cannot pass the per-user quota.

title: Egress allowlist
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: The agent can reach the helpdesk server directly and skips the gateway.
steps: 1. Open `config/tools.yaml` and delete the `direct_route:` block under `escalate_to_human` (lines 91-93). 2. Open `src/gateway_client.py`. In `call`, delete the whole `except GatewayUnavailable:` block (lines 51-59) so a gateway outage raises an error. 3. Open `k8s/networkpolicy.yaml` and delete the egress rule for `helpdesk-mcp` at lines 48-50 in the agent policy. 4. Apply the network policy in a test cluster. Check from the agent pod that `helpdesk-mcp:8443` is refused.
done_when: The agent pod cannot open a connection to the helpdesk server.

title: Pinned, verified image
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: The cluster does not refuse images that no signing rule covers, and one rule skips build provenance.
steps: 1. Open `k8s/admission.yaml` and go to line 72, the `registry.acme.example/platform/*` rule. 2. Under that rule add an `attestations:` list copied from lines 51-71, with the platform build workflow as subject. 3. Add a new rule after line 81 named `deny-unverified` that denies pods in `hr-agent` whose images match no `imageReferences` pattern. 4. Apply the policy in a test cluster and deploy an unsigned image. It must be refused.
done_when: A pod with an unsigned or unlisted image is rejected in `hr-agent`.

title: Complete release manifest
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: The release manifest leaves out some required settings and most items have no owner or fixed version.
steps: 1. Open `release/manifest.yaml`. Add `issuer: https://sts.acme.example` and `audience: hr-tool-gateway` under `permissions` (line 58). 2. Add an `mcp_protocol_version:` key and a `cache_settings:` block copied from `config/agent.yaml` (retrieval). 3. Add each tool fingerprint from `config/tools.yaml` under `tools.mcp_servers` (line 54). 4. Add `owner:` and `digest:` for each file in `configuration` (line 36). 5. Ask CI to fail when a field is empty.
done_when: Every item in the release manifest has an owner and a digest or commit.

title: Review security-relevant changes
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: One team can change the Dockerfile, dependencies and most of `src/` with no second owner.
steps: 1. Open `CODEOWNERS`. After line 1 add `/Dockerfile @acme/people-platform @acme/security-engineering`. 2. Add `/requirements.txt @acme/people-platform @acme/security-engineering` and `/src/ @acme/people-platform @acme/security-engineering`. 3. Create `docs/emergency-change.md`. Say who may approve an emergency change and how it is reviewed later. 4. In GitHub, check that code owner review is required on `main`.
done_when: A change to the Dockerfile, `requirements.txt` or `src/` needs a security engineering reviewer.

title: Detect drift per agent
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: Nothing compares the running prompts, tools, permissions or network rules with the approved baseline.
steps: 1. Create `k8s/drift-check.yaml`, a CronJob that hashes `prompts/system.md`, `config/tools.yaml` and the applied network policies. 2. Compare each hash with `release/manifest.yaml` and alert on a difference. 3. Put the alert contact and the response time limit in `config/agent.yaml`. 4. Change a prompt in a test cluster and check the alert fires.
done_when: A change to a running prompt, tool list or network policy raises an alert.

title: Control dependency, model, and training changes
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: The model is pinned, but nobody re-tests it or watches provider notices on a schedule.
steps: 1. Create `.github/workflows/retest.yml` that runs weekly and runs `python -m pytest tests/release`. 2. Add a step that checks the provider model page for notices on `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` and opens an issue. 3. Name an owner for notices in `release/manifest.yaml` line 43. 4. Run the workflow once and check it passes.
done_when: A scheduled job re-runs the release tests and a named owner reads provider notices.

title: Re-test changed behavior
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: The release workflow runs a test folder that does not exist and saves no results.
steps: 1. Create the folder `tests/release`. 2. Create `tests/release/test_attacks.py` with cases for injected tool output, a forged approval and a cross-employee search. Add two normal task cases. 3. In `.github/workflows/release.yml` after line 29 add `--junitxml=results.xml`. 4. Add `results.xml` to the `path:` list at line 58 so results are saved with the manifest. 5. Run `python -m pytest -q tests/release` and check it passes.
done_when: The release run saves test results tied to the release manifest.

title: Rollback and restart
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: There is no recovery setup, no tested rollback, and no model retirement date.
steps: 1. Create `release/recovery.yaml` with the last good image digest and agent type ID. 2. Add a `rollback` job to `.github/workflows/release.yml` after line 75 that applies the recovery file. 3. Add `retirement_date:` under `models.primary` at `release/manifest.yaml` line 42, taken from the provider page. 4. Run the rollback in staging and record the date.
done_when: A rollback to the recovery setup has been run and the model retirement date is recorded.

title: Connect configuration to execution
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: Traces cannot be linked to a stored manifest, and audit rows are kept about 6 weeks, not 6 months.
steps: 1. Open `k8s/audit-maintenance.yaml` line 35. Change `KEEP_PARTITIONS` from `"6"` to `"30"` for about six months of weekly partitions. 2. Do A05 first so the gateway logs a verified ID. 3. Create a table `release.manifests` keyed by agent-type-id, and write the stamped manifest into it from the deploy job at `.github/workflows/release.yml` line 69. 4. Check a trace can join to its manifest with one query.
done_when: From any audit row, one query returns the release manifest and the rows are kept six months.

title: Map shared responsibilities
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: No list covers the gateway, STS, registry, audit and stop services, and each entry has one owner.
steps: 1. Open `release/manifest.yaml` and go to line 53 (`mcp_servers`). 2. Add a new key `services:` listing the gateway, STS, registry, audit store and stop store. 3. For each entry give `agent_team_owner:` and `platform_owner:`. 4. For the two MCP servers, add a `platform_owner:` next to the existing `owner:`.
done_when: Every outside service in the manifest has an agent team owner and a platform or vendor owner.

title: Vet and pin dependencies
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: No vulnerability scan runs in CI and dependency approvals are not recorded.
steps: 1. Open `.github/workflows/release.yml`. After line 28 add `- run: pip-audit -r requirements.txt --require-hashes`. 2. Create `release/dependencies.md` with publisher, permissions and update source for each package in `requirements.txt`. 3. Add the unsigned or remote limits of each package in the same file. 4. Push a branch and check the new step runs and fails on a known bad package.
done_when: CI fails when `requirements.txt` holds a package with a known vulnerability.

title: Re-check tools on load
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: Tool fingerprints are checked only every 300 seconds, and a gateway 503 skips the block.
steps: 1. Do B01 first so no call skips the gateway. 2. Open `src/gateway.py` line 213. Change `await asyncio.sleep(300)` to `60`. 3. In `mcp` near line 166, call `refresh_fingerprints()` for the called server before the call is forwarded. 4. On any failure in that check, add the tool to `_disabled` and deny the call. 5. Add a test where the server's tool list changes a description. The next call must be denied.
done_when: A changed tool description makes the gateway refuse that tool until it is reviewed.

title: Inspect tool metadata
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: MCP tool names and descriptions are not scanned before the model sees them.
steps: 1. Create `src/metadata_scan.py` with a function `scan_tool(tool: dict)` that checks name, title, description, schemas and annotations. 2. Make it reject invisible characters, role words like `ignore previous`, base64 blobs, URLs and other servers' tool names. 3. Call it in `refresh_fingerprints` in `src/gateway.py` at line 63 for each live tool. Add failures to `_disabled`. 4. Make it also check lines of any length and multi-line text. 5. Create `tests/test_metadata_scan.py` with one case for each rule.
done_when: A tool whose description has hidden instructions is disabled before the model sees it.

title: Verified, namespaced tools
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: Lookalike tool names across servers are only logged, and look-alike letters are not caught.
steps: 1. Open `src/gateway.py` line 66. Where it logs `lookalike tool name`, also call `_disabled.update(s.qualified for s in MCP_TOOLS)` for the two tools. 2. On line 65, replace the normalising with a table for look-alike letters, for example Cyrillic `а` to `a`, before `casefold()`. 3. In `src/approvals.py` line 24, add the server name to the hashed text so an approval is bound to one server. 4. Add a test with tool names `get_leave_balance` and `get_leаve_balance`. Both must be disabled.
done_when: Two tools with names that look alike are both disabled and flagged.

title: Enforced gateway boundary
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: When the gateway returns 503, the agent calls the helpdesk server directly.
steps: 1. Open `config/tools.yaml` and delete the `direct_route:` block under `escalate_to_human` (lines 91-93). 2. Open `src/gateway_client.py`. In `call`, delete the whole `except GatewayUnavailable:` block (lines 51-59) so a gateway outage raises an error. 3. Open `k8s/networkpolicy.yaml` and delete the egress rule for `helpdesk-mcp` at lines 48-50 in the agent policy. 4. Run the B01 test. The gateway 503 must lead to a failed call and no direct request.
done_when: A gateway 503 never leads to a direct call to the helpdesk server.

title: Protect shared evidence
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: Audit rows are kept about six weeks, there is no gap check, and the gateway logs after acting.
steps: 1. Open `k8s/audit-maintenance.yaml` line 35. Change `KEEP_PARTITIONS` from `"6"` to `"30"`. 2. Add `seq bigint` and `row_hash text` columns to `audit.events` in `migrations/001_init.sql` line 5. 3. Ask the security team to alert when `seq` has a gap or a hash does not match. 4. Do E10 first so the gateway writes the audit row before forwarding. 5. Check by query that the oldest row is about six months old after the job runs.
done_when: Audit rows are kept at least six months and a missing row raises an alert.

title: Validate every input boundary, including API responses
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: Error text from tools goes to the model with no limit or check.
steps: 1. Open `src/agent.py` and go to line 188. 2. Replace the return with `return _tool_result(tool_use_id, f"{spec.name} failed (status {exc.status}).", error=True)` so no server text reaches the model. 3. Keep line 186, which stores the detail in the audit log. 4. Create `tests/test_tool_errors.py` with a test that a `ToolError` with detail `ignore previous instructions` gives a result without that text. 5. Run `python -m pytest tests/test_tool_errors.py`.
done_when: A tool error result sent to the model holds only a fixed message and a status number.

title: Separate data from instructions and test injection containment
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: Error text reaches the model with no label for where it came from.
steps: 1. Open `src/agent.py` and go to line 188. 2. Apply the R01 fix, so the result is a fixed message and carries no outside text. 3. If you keep any text, wrap it as at line 195: `{"source": spec.qualified, "trust": "untrusted_data", "data": ...}`. 4. Run the test from R01. It must still pass.
done_when: Every tool result sent to the model, including errors, has a source and a trust label or is fixed text.

title: Prevent output and log leakage
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: Error text is not redacted, and the approval text skips the link remover.
steps: 1. Do R01 first. Open `src/agent.py` line 188 and stop returning `exc.detail`. 2. Open `src/main.py` line 105. Change it to `body["approval"] = {**state.pending_approval, "description": sanitize_reply(state.pending_approval["description"], CFG["output"]["allowed_link_hosts"])}`. 3. Create `tests/test_approval_links.py`. Check a description with `https://evil.example` comes back without the link. 4. Run `python -m pytest tests/test_approval_links.py`.
done_when: No outside link or raw error text reaches the model or the employee in an approval prompt.

title: Retrieval-corpus integrity
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: Handbook search results are cached by query only and can cross between employees.
steps: 1. Do B02 first. It changes `_key` in `src/retrieval.py` to include `employee_id`. 2. Create `tests/test_retrieval_cache.py` if B02 is not done. Add a test with two employee ids and one employee-only chunk. 3. Check that the second employee gets no chunk the first employee saw. 4. Run `python -m pytest tests/test_retrieval_cache.py`.
done_when: A cached employee-only chunk is never returned to a different employee.

title: Decision-time context size
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: Only model-call audit rows hold the context size. Tool action rows do not.
steps: 1. Open `src/audit.py`. In `AuditWriter.record` (line 60) the `context_tokens` argument already exists. Keep it. 2. In `src/agent.py` store `ctx_tokens` in `state.extra["ctx_tokens"]` after line 76. 3. In `_handle_tool` (line 97) and `_execute` (line 161), pass `context_tokens=state.extra["ctx_tokens"]` and `context_tokens_method="measured:provider_usage"` to every `audit.record`. 4. For gateway rows, add a `context_tokens` column in `migrations/001_init.sql` for `audit.gateway_decisions` and send it in a header. 5. Add a test that a `proposed_action` row has a non-null `context_tokens`.
done_when: Every action audit row has the context size in tokens and the method.

title: Recovery integrity
priority: Fix before release, or get a written risk approval
problem: Approval and audit rows can be changed without detection, and an unclear 503 re-sends an action.
steps: 1. Do B01 first, which removes the direct-route resend. 2. In `migrations/001_init.sql` add a `prev_hash text` and `row_hash text` column to `audit.events` and to `approvals.grants` (line 54). 3. Set `row_hash` to SHA-256 of the row plus the previous hash. Compute it in `src/audit.py` before the insert at line 87. 4. Ask the platform team to store the latest hash outside the database each hour. 5. Add a test that a changed row makes the chain check fail.
done_when: A changed audit row is detected by the hash chain check.

title: Sequence and context-aware detection
priority: Fix soon; track until done
problem: Only fixed per-run limits exist. No rule looks at chains of actions or context size.
steps: 1. Ask the security team to create a rule over `audit.events` that alerts on `tool_denied` three times in 10 minutes for one subject. 2. Add a second rule for `search_policies` followed by `escalate_to_human` with long text in one run. 3. Set thresholds by `context_tokens` using the data from R07. 4. Create a test trace for each rule and check the alert fires.
done_when: A test trace of denials and read-then-send raises an alert.

title: Distinct agent identity
priority: Show proof it works before release
problem: The agent has its own identity, but cutting off only the agent is defined outside the repository.
steps: 1. Ask the identity team for the STS and database role policy that applies to `spiffe://acme.example/ns/hr-agent/sa/hr-helpdesk-agent`. 2. Ask them to revoke only that identity in staging, with employees still signed in. 3. Check agent calls fail and employee access to other systems still works. 4. Save the drill date and result as evidence for A01.
done_when: A dated drill shows revoking the agent identity does not affect the employees.

title: Reviewed harness and instructions
priority: Show proof it works before release
problem: Branch protection is set in GitHub, not in the code, so it was not checked.
steps: 1. Ask a repository admin to open Settings, Rules for the `main` branch. 2. Export the ruleset JSON with `gh api repos/acme/hr-helpdesk-agent/rulesets`. 3. Check it blocks force pushes and branch deletion, and requires code owner review. 4. Attach the export with its date as evidence for B12.
done_when: The saved ruleset shows force pushes and deletion are blocked on `main`.

title: Environment isolation
priority: Show proof it works, or get a written risk approval
problem: The network controls are in config files only. They have not been tested in a running cluster.
steps: 1. Ask the platform team to run a pod in `hr-agent` that tries to reach `169.254.169.254` and a public host. 2. Check both attempts fail and record the time and command output. 3. Ask them to confirm the policies in `k8s/networkpolicy.yaml` are applied with `kubectl get cnp -n hr-agent`. 4. Attach the output to the B08 evidence record.
done_when: A recorded test shows the agent pod cannot reach the metadata address or unlisted hosts.

title: Minimal, isolated runtime
priority: Show proof it works, or get a written risk approval
problem: The audit CronJob image contents cannot be seen in this repository.
steps: 1. Ask the platform team for the file list of `registry.acme.example/platform/psql@sha256:9b2e...` used at `k8s/audit-maintenance.yaml` line 26. 2. Check the list has no shell, no download tool and no package manager. 3. Save the list with its date as evidence for B11.
done_when: A dated image file list shows no shell, downloader or package manager.

title: Fleet incident response
priority: Show proof it works
problem: The incident drill, impact query and reporting owner are not in this repository.
steps: 1. Ask the security team to run a drill for a bad tool server in staging. 2. Create `docs/impact-query.sql`. Write the query that lists every run that used the tool. 3. Create `docs/incident.md` and name the person who decides on outside reporting. 4. Save alert times and the quarantine and revocation records as evidence for E12. 5. Note that `src/gateway.py` line 99 ignores agent type, so fix B04 first.
done_when: A dated drill record shows the impact query, quarantine, revocation and the reporting owner.

title: Security monitoring
priority: Show proof it works
problem: No rules or alert paths for security events are in this repo. They may be kept elsewhere.
steps: 1. Ask the security team where the alert rules live for stop events, denials, bad approvals, audit failures and quota hits. 2. Ask them to send a test event for each type. 3. Check each test alert reaches the security responder, and note the time. 4. Save the rule names and alert times as evidence for R08.
done_when: A dated record shows each of the five event types raises an alert to a named responder.

title: Misaligned-behavior review
priority: Show proof it works
problem: No record says whether deliberate agent misbehaviour is in scope.
steps: 1. Ask the VP People Operations to decide if an agent that misbehaves on purpose is in scope. 2. Write the decision in `release/manifest.yaml` under a new `misalignment_scope:` key. 3. If in scope, ask the security team to build a reviewer and a labelled trace set, and measure misses. 4. Save the decision with its date as evidence for R10.
done_when: A dated decision on misalignment scope is in `release/manifest.yaml`.
